Radiation Oncology Guidelines For Special Techniques > Brachytherapy of the Coronary Arteries > DISCUSSION (TOC: S3.5.3)

Required findings: Diagnosis of in-stent restenosis (ISR) in a native coronary artery or saphenous vein graft (SVG) stent
Procedure is used as an adjunct to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)
Patient is not a candidate for repeat drug-eluting stents (DES) or bypass surgery (for recurrent ISR)
Single treatment of coronary artery brachytherapy
Medical necessity indications.Source: Radiation Oncology Guidelines For Special Techniques > Brachytherapy of the Coronary Arteries (TOC: S3.5)

Non-Indications: Treatment for new stenosis of native coronary arteries and saphenous vein grafts (SVGs)
Restenosis of native coronary arteries and SVGs at the unstented site of a previous PCI
Primary prevention of restenosis after stent implantation for de novo lesions
Any indication other than adjunct to PCI for ISR in native coronary arteries or SVGs, or recurrent ISR where patient is not a candidate for repeat DES or bypass surgery
Important criteria & exceptions: Drug-eluting stents (DES) are the preferred method of treatment for in-stent restenosis; brachytherapy is considered a Level 2b recommendation by ACC/AHA/SCAI for patients with recurrent ISR in arteries unfavorable for another DES or who are not good candidates for bypass surgery

European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines recommend brachytherapy for ISR in native coronary arteries (Class 1A) and SVGs (Class 1B), noting that prolonged intake of clopidogrel for 1 year after radiation is necessary
There is insufficient evidence to demonstrate safety and efficacy for expanded indications such as de novo lesion prevention or unstented site restenosis
Documentation required: Clinical documentation confirming diagnosis of in-stent restenosis (ISR) in a native coronary artery or saphenous vein graft (SVG)
Documentation that the patient is not a candidate for repeat drug-eluting stents (DES) or bypass surgery (if applicable for recurrent ISR)
Confirmation that the procedure is being used as an adjunct to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)
